Weekly Dispatch #42

Good morning. This week we look at why independent magazines are quietly thriving, and what the numbers say about attention in the age of the infinite scroll. It turns out the constraint is the feature: a finite object, read to the end, remembered.

The finite object

Consider the difference between a stack of open tabs and a stapled booklet on the kitchen table. One is a to-do list; the other is a promise kept. Readers consistently report finishing print issues at rates digital archives never approach, and the psychology is simple: an ending is a gift.

Print subscriptions for small magazines grew again this year, up double digits for the fifth year running, driven mostly by niche titles under 10,000 subscribers with fiercely loyal readerships.

What we're reading

A wonderful essay on marginalia; an interview with a letterpress printer who refuses to retire; and a data dive into why finishing rates matter more than open rates for anything you actually want to remember.

See you next week. — The Dispatch team
